title: Minority Prophet Claim Warrant
description: A typed warrant attached to a ledger node's `evidence` object. It records how a node's assertion could be checked, not whether it is true. Deliberately local: no field is imported from any external package, and nothing here is fetched at runtime. The four-way typology follows the classical pramanas (perception, inference, comparison, testimony); the modern formulation borrowed from is Kadaboina 2026, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20283647, Apache-2.0. Nothing in this schema validates that work's formal claims. PLACEMENT IS NORMATIVE: this object is stored under the single reserved key `claim_warrant` inside a node's `evidence` object, never flattened into it. `resolvable_reference()` inspects `evidence` values to decide whether a parentless claim names anything checkable, and `UnattributedRootError` is a hard gate on that result. A warrant's `source_digest` is a hex string matching the accepted `hash` form, so a flattened warrant could satisfy that gate and admit a root that was previously refused. A warrant describes how a claim could be checked; it is not itself evidence that the claim named anything. Metadata must never satisfy the gate.

warrant_version.description: Schema version of this warrant object.

claim_type.description: The epistemic ground the node's assertion rests on.

verify_determinism.description: DERIVED, never author-supplied. `measured` and `cited` are deterministic: re-checkable mechanically without a judge. `inferred` and `analogized` are oracle_conditional: checking requires a theorem prover, structural matcher, fixed-metric oracle, or LLM. A producer that sets this inconsistently with claim_type is malformed; consumers recompute rather than trust it.

verify_outcome.description: Result of an actual re-check, if one was performed. THREE-VALUED BY DESIGN. `unverifiable` must never be collapsed into `rejected`: a claim whose source has become unreachable is not a claim that failed, and the difference is exactly the signal false-prophet screening depends on. A prophet can make claims unverifiable at no cost.

reason.description: Why. For `unverifiable`, the distinguishing detail: fetch_failed, not_decodable, digest_malformed, oracle_absent, sla_timeout.

checked_by.description: Identifier of the checker. Not necessarily the node's observer.

source_digest.description: Hash of the source bytes as observed when the assertion was made, if any. Optional and frequently absent: presence is what makes an offline re-check possible, so its absence must be recorded rather than assumed away. Never surfaced to resolvable_reference(): see the normative placement rule above.

recheck_reference.description: Where a re-check would go. A URI for a citation, a method identifier for a measurement. Free-form: this schema does not constrain external vocabularies.

external_attestation.description: Opaque passthrough for an externally-produced attestation the warrant was derived from. Stored for audit, never interpreted by the ledger. Kept unconstrained so no external schema becomes a dependency of this one.
